contentBlocks.text: This week you've learned about representation gaps and their power when done right. Today: your own real part in it!

There are real, everyday ways a student can help improve representation, connecting directly back to last week's civic-engagement lesson: writing an accurate short description of Sikh identity for a school project, politely and confidently correcting a classmate's honest misconception (the same confident-explaining skill from last week), or recommending an accurate book or resource to a teacher or librarian. Write a short plan for one specific, realistic way you could help improve representation at your own school.
You just made your own real plan to help improve representation! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Identify realistic, everyday ways a student can help improve representation
Write a specific personal plan connected to the child's own school
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's representation-gap and power-of-representation lessons.
2. Introduce realistic student-level ways to help, connecting back to last week's confident-explaining and civic-engagement skills.
3. Have the child write their own specific, realistic plan.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer the three example actions from the lesson as a menu to choose from rather than requiring an original idea
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one way an entire class, not just one student, could help improve representation together
This is the week's synthesis and empowerment moment — connecting representation directly to last week's civic-engagement content is the genuinely important thread here
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended activity — check that the child's plan is specific and realistic (a real project, conversation, or recommendation they could actually attempt), not vague or generic.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's civic-engagement and representation threads together, closing this week's thread with a genuine student-empowerment action before tomorrow's review.

generationData.instructions: Write your specific plan to help improve representation at your school.
